designSummary: Single-site diagnostic accuracy study; 2 by 2 table of the month-3 cut-off against separation within 12 months of hire.
sampleSize: About 280 residents are expected across four intakes. At 20 percent separation, about 56 residents will separate and 224 will stay. With an expected sensitivity of 0.70, 56 separations give a 95 percent confidence interval of about plus or minus 0.12 (1.96 x sqrt(0.70 x 0.30 / 56)); an expected specificity of 0.68 with 224 stayers gives about plus or minus 0.06. A half-width of 0.10 for sensitivity would need about 81 separations, roughly six intakes; the team accepts plus or minus 0.12 for a local decision about the booster and will report the intervals as they are.
primaryAnalysis: Sensitivity and specificity at 30 or below with Wilson 95 percent confidence intervals, from all residents with both a month-3 score and a 12-month reference-standard result; STARD flow diagram.
secondaryAnalysis: Area under the ROC curve for the continuous score with a DeLong interval; positive and negative predictive values at the observed separation rate and recalculated at 19 and 26 percent; accuracy by rotation pattern and campus reported descriptively.
missingData: Residents with an incomplete check or withdrawn consent are counted in the flow diagram; no imputation. A missing separation date is treated as staying only after human resources confirms continued employment.
multiplicity: One pre-specified cut-off carries the question; other cut-offs and subgroups are exploratory and labelled as such.
software: R; the analysis script and the cut-off are archived before the first reference-standard extract is released.
overfittingGuards: Cut-off fixed before linkage; no threshold optimisation in the same data
Youden index reported only as exploratory
Analysis script archived before the first extract
summary: About 56 separations give sensitivity to plus or minus 0.12 and specificity to plus or minus 0.06 at the pre-specified cut-off.
